**Definition**
- Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) is a process that allows students to earn academic credit for college-level knowledge and skills gained outside the traditional classroom. This can include work experience, military training, professional certifications, or other relevant life experiences.

**Key Points**
- PLA helps students graduate faster and save money by awarding credit for what they already know.
- PLA options and policies may vary by program. Not all programs offer PLA.

**How It Works**
- Students typically submit documentation (such as certifications, training records, or portfolios) for evaluation.
- An advisor or faculty member reviews the materials to determine if they meet the criteria for academic credit.

**For TTU Online+**

TTU Online offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate degrees designed for flexibility, accessibility, and career alignment, delivered in accelerated 8-week formats. We have programs in the social sciences, pre-health, business, leadership, communication, etc.

Can I take online and on-campus classes at the same time?

TTU Online only offers asynchronous 8-week online courses. There are some programs traditional programs through TTU Lubbock that have both on-campus and online course options.

Can I study online while working full-time?

Absolutely. Texas Tech Online offers flexible Online+ programs (opens in new tab) designed for working adults.

Link for "Online+ programs (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/programs/?subNav=Online%2B

Would Online+ be better for me since I work full time and I cannot attend class in person? Can I take all my classes online from the beginning of college?

The Texas Tech Online+ program is designed specifically for working professionals, providing the flexibility to complete your coursework fully online. This makes it an excellent choice for individuals who work full-time and cannot attend classes in person. You can take all your classes online from the beginning of your studies, as the program offers various online degree options that can accommodate your schedule. If you're interested in learning more or getting started with the Online+ program, please visit http://GoOnline.ttu.edu (opens in new tab) or contact them directly at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

Can I earn credit for work and life experience?

Yes! Online+ offers free prior learning assessments (PLA) that allow you to earn credit for professional certifications, military training and work experience—helping you graduate faster and save money.

Would Online+ be a good fit for a student that was not yet mature enough to go to college earlier in life but is now ready to commit to education?

Yes, the Online+ program at Texas Tech University would be a great fit for a student who may not have been ready for college earlier in life but is now committed to pursuing their education. The program is designed specifically for non-traditional students, including those looking to balance their studies with work and life commitments. It offers flexibility with eight-week accelerated courses and asynchronous learning, allowing students to study on their own schedule. Additionally, the program recognizes prior work-life experiences, making it easier for students to earn credit and complete their degree. If you're interested in getting started or want more information, you can visit http://GoOnline.ttu.edu (opens in new tab) or contact the TTU Online+ program at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

Are all of the online programs at TTU 8 weeks long?

No, Online+ programs use 8-week terms, while some traditional programs may still follow 16-week formats.

Are courses for the TTU Online+ programs completely asynchronous?

Yes, all Online+ courses are designed to be flexible and asynchronous.

answer.text:
**TTU Online+ Programs Offering PLA (Prior Learning Assessment) Credit**

- TTU Online+ offers PLA credit options in many of its programs, especially those designed for working professionals, adult learners, and degree completion pathways.
- PLA is most prominently featured in:
  - **10K Degree Completion Program** (Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies, Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies)
    - Up to 9 credit hours for prior work/life experience
    - Up to 21 hours when combined with free microcredentials
  - **Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences (BAAS) Degrees**
    - Applied Leadership, Human Sciences, Emergency Management, Legal Studies, Renewable Energy
    - Designed to maximize transfer and prior learning credit
  - **Other Online+ Bachelor’s Degrees**
    - Many bachelor’s programs (such as General Studies, Human Sciences, and Interdisciplinary Studies) allow for PLA, but the number of credits and eligibility are determined on a case-by-case basis.

**Key Points:**
- PLA is not guaranteed in every program; it is most common in flexible, adult-learner-focused, and degree completion programs.
- Graduate programs may offer PLA in limited cases, but this is less common and must be confirmed with an advisor.

**How to Confirm for Your Program:**
- Contact an Enrollment Service Specialist to review your prior learning and determine PLA eligibility for your specific program:  
  [Enrollment Service Specialist (opens in new tab)](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/advocates/)
- You can also reach TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu for personalized guidance.

**Next Step:**  
If you have a specific program in mind, let me know and I can check PLA availability for that program.

**Difference Between an M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies vs. an M.S. in Interdisciplinary Sciences (TTU Online+)**

At Texas Tech University Online+, both degrees are interdisciplinary master’s programs, but they differ in focus and coursework requirements:

---

**Master of Arts (M.A.) in Interdisciplinary Studies**
- Best for students whose primary academic interests are in non-STEM fields.
- Combines approved disciplines into a cohesive, customizable plan of study.
- Emphasizes humanities, social sciences, arts, and related areas.

**Master of Science (M.S.) in Interdisciplinary Sciences**
- Requires at least 18 credit hours of approved STEM coursework.
- Ideal for students seeking an interdisciplinary foundation rooted in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics.
- Emphasizes STEM disciplines and scientific approaches.

---

**Summary Table**

| Degree | Focus | Coursework Requirement |
|--------|-------|-----------------------|
| M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies | Non-STEM fields (humanities, social sciences, arts) | Flexible, based on chosen disciplines |
| M.S. in Interdisciplinary Sciences | STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, math) | At least 18 credit hours in STEM |

---

**Next Step:**  
For more details, see the [Degree and Course Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=16541) or contact an academic advisor for guidance on which option best fits your goals.

**Commonly Asked Questions About the TTU Online+ Graduate Program**

---

**Program Structure & Format**
- **What is the 8-week Online+ model?**  
  The Online+ model delivers graduate courses in accelerated 8-week terms, allowing students to focus on fewer courses at a time and progress efficiently toward degree completion. All courses are 100% online and asynchronous.

- **Are courses synchronous?**  
  No, all Online+ courses are fully asynchronous with no required live sessions.

- **How many courses can I take per term?**  
  Most students take 1–2 courses per 8-week term. Full-time status is 6 credit hours per term.

---

**Admissions & Enrollment**
- **How do I apply?**  
  Applications are completed online: [Apply Here](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/apply/).

- **What are the admission requirements?**  
  Requirements vary by program but generally include prior academic records and GPA criteria.

- **Can I enroll at any time?**  
  Online+ offers multiple start dates throughout the year.

---

**Cost, Financial Aid & Scholarships**
- **How much does the program cost?**  
  Tuition is charged per credit hour. Use the [Tuition Estimator](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/studentbusinessservices/feeinfo/tuition-estimator.php) for details.

- **Is financial aid available?**  
  Yes, students may qualify for federal aid, grants, scholarships, and military benefits.  
  Contact: Online.Finaid@ttu.edu

- **Are scholarships offered?**  
  Yes, eligible students can apply for scholarships. Visit [TTU Online+ Financial Aid & Scholarships](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/financial-aid/) for details.

---

**Student Experience & Support**
- **Will I have access to support services?**  
  Yes, Online+ students receive academic advising, Online Student Advocates, tutoring, writing center support, technical support, and student success resources.

- **Is this format manageable for working professionals?**  
  Yes, the asynchronous structure is designed for students balancing work, family, and other commitments.

---

**Coursework & Academic Policies**
- **How many hours per term is full-time?**  
  Full-time is 6 credit hours per 8-week term.

- **Can I transfer credits?**  
  Yes, transfer credits are evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

- **Will my diploma say “Online”?**  
  No, your diploma and transcript will say “Texas Tech University.”

---

**Technology**
- **What technology is required?**  
  Reliable internet, a supported web browser, and a computer capable of streaming video and uploading assignments.

---

**Graduation**
- **Can online students participate in commencement?**  
  Yes, online students are eligible and encouraged to participate in graduation ceremonies.

---

**Need More Help?**
- Contact TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu  
- [TTU Online+ Programs Page](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/programs/)

Launch your accounting career and meet CPA exam requirements with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Professional Accounting. This 30-hour program builds core accounting expertise and prepares you for professional practice and licensure success.

The Online Master of Professional Accounting (MPAcc) at Texas Tech University is a 30-credit-hour graduate program launching in fall 2026, designed for students without an undergraduate accounting degree who want to pursue professional accounting careers and satisfy CPA exam requirements. The curriculum maps to core content areas tested on the CPA exam — including Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR), Auditing and Attestation (AUD), Taxation and Regulation (REG) and Information Systems and Controls (ISC) — while developing technical proficiency and professional competencies needed in public accounting, industry and non-profit environments. Students study taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, advanced accounting topics, ethics and business law. Delivered fully online and asynchronously, the program provides flexibility for working professionals and prepares graduates to excel as accounting practitioners, leaders and strategic contributors in a wide range of organizations.

Prerequisites: ACCT 3305, ACCT 4300, ACCT 4301, ACCT 5302, ISQS 2340. Corequisite: ACCT 5303. Learn strategies related to advanced database and querying skills in addition to expanding on forensic accounting topics and financial information modeling techniques.

The 30-hour Master of Arts in Mass Communication program is designed to prepare students to succeed in the communications industry or to continue studies toward a Doctor of Philosophy degree. Depending upon courses selected, graduate students are prepared for careers and advanced study in media and communication fields, journalism, publishing, advertising, public relations, and other related industries.

Students in the Mass Communication master's program are offered two curriculum options: a traditional research-based thesis track or a professional non-thesis track. Both tracks are 30 credit hours.

The thesis track requires 24 hours of coursework and a minimum of six hours of thesis credit. The thesis is comprehensive original research and typically takes a full summer or regular semester to complete. Coursework must include three required courses: MCOM 5366, MCOM 5364 and MCOM 5374.

The professional non-thesis track includes two required courses, seven elective courses and concludes with a capstone final project course, MCOM 6050. This course will be taken in the student's final semester and will require the completion of an applied research project. The sports media focus is an option within the professional program that includes not only coursework but also an internship in a sports communication setting.

**Online Master of Professional Accounting (MPAcc) at Texas Tech University**

**Program Overview**
- 30 credit-hour graduate program launching in Fall 2026
- Designed for students without an undergraduate accounting degree
- Prepares you for professional accounting careers and CPA exam requirements
- Curriculum covers core CPA exam content: Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR), Auditing and Attestation (AUD), Taxation and Regulation (REG), Information Systems and Controls (ISC)
- Develops technical proficiency and professional competencies for public accounting, industry, and non-profit sectors
- Delivered fully online and asynchronously for working professionals

**Prerequisites**
- Bachelor’s degree required
- Completion of intermediate accounting sequence (ACCT 3304 and 3305)

**Key Courses**
- ACCT 5302: Introduction to Data and Analytics for Accountants
- ACCT 5319: Auditing Theory and Practice
- ACCT 5332: Ethics in Accounting
- ACCT 5321: Advanced Data and Analytics for Accountants
- ACCT 5309: Advanced Accounting
- ACCT 5327: Advanced Income Taxation Accounting
- ACCT 5392: Advanced Business Law
- ACCT 5308: Federal Income Tax Law for Partnerships
